change.title: pr-1-flat
change.description: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Default audit-log path now crashes when the caller has no membership
findings.body: `enable_advanced` is computed on every request, before `use_optimized` is checked. `organization_context.member` is `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346). It is None whenever `request.user.id` has no membership: `convert_args` passes `user_id=request.user.id` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:285-291), and that id is None for key-authenticated requests. For any such caller that isn't a superuser, `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError, so the endpoint returns 500 even when `optimized_pagination` is absent. Before this change, that request worked. Fix: check `use_optimized` first, and guard the member, e.g. `member = organization_context.member; enable_advanced = is_active_superuser(request) or (member is not None and member.has_global_access)`.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator returns 500 for every non-empty audit-log page
findings.body:
The endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `self.key` is `datetime`. `get_item_key` is copied from the integer `Paginator` and calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a `datetime`, which raises TypeError. `build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])` and `key(results[-1])` whenever there are results (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-137, 197). So `?optimized_pagination=true` returns 500 for any org that has audit entries.

`value_from_cursor` (line 843) has a related problem: it passes the raw millisecond integer into `build_queryset`, which compares it against a timestamp column (line 119-126). That breaks every cursor-based request too. `DateTimePaginator` converts in both places (lines 233-241). Subclass `DateTimePaginator` instead of `BasePaginator`, or reuse its key and value conversion.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch cannot work: Django rejects negative QuerySet slices
findings.body:
`queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` in Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__`. So any cursor like `0:-5:0` sent by an admin with `optimized_pagination=true` returns 500. The comment's claim that "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. The same is true of the `else` branch at line 884 for prev cursors (`offset` is passed through unclamped).

The stated purpose, "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", isn't a valid goal for a paginator either. If this were ever changed to slice a materialized list, the meaning of the cursor offset would silently change. Remove the branch and clamp the offset to >= 0 in every case, or reject a negative offset with a 400 when the cursor is parsed.

findings.title: Gate uses `request.user.is_superuser` and `has_global_access`, so it doesn't mean "authorized administrators"
findings.body: `request.user.is_superuser` is true even without an active superuser session. The permission class for this endpoint uses `is_active_superuser(request)` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:124). Also, `OrganizationMember.has_global_access` defaults to True (src/sentry/models/organizationmember.py:216), so in practice the gate is open to almost any member who already passed the `org:write` check. Use `is_active_superuser(request)`. If admin-only access is really intended, check the role or scopes explicitly.

findings.title: Comment in the shared BasePaginator is false
findings.body: The comment says negative offsets are allowed and that "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions". The code clamps only non-prev cursors to 0. For prev cursors it still passes a negative offset to the QuerySet slice, and Django raises ValueError there. Clamping the forward path is a harmless improvement for all `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` users. Reword the comment to describe that, and clamp the prev path too, or reject negative offsets.

findings.title: Comment describes behaviour the line doesn't implement
findings.body: `self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged and already accepted negative values. The new comment suggests a deliberate feature ("efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions") that doesn't exist; no paginator can slice with a negative offset. Remove the comment.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds no tests. A single test of `GET` audit logs with `optimized_pagination=true` against an org with at least one entry would have caught the TypeError in `get_item_key`. A test with a member-less caller would have caught the AttributeError on the default path.

findings.title: `get_result` duplicates BasePaginator.get_result almost verbatim
findings.body: Apart from the negative-offset branch, which can't work, lines 845-911 repeat `BasePaginator.get_result` line for line. Once that branch is removed, the class adds nothing over `DateTimePaginator`, and the endpoint could keep using `DateTimePaginator` alone.

contracts.equivalent_path: OrganizationAuditPermission.has_object_permission falls back to is_active_superuser(request) without touching member
contracts.before_after: Before: the endpoint never dereferenced member. After: it dereferences it unconditionally unless request.user.is_superuser.
contracts.visible_effect: 500 for callers whose context has member=None
contracts.failure_mode: AttributeError on NoneType when member is None (user_id None or no membership)

contracts.action: Paginate audit logs with OptimizedCursorPaginator when optimized_pagination=true
contracts.equivalent_path: DateTimePaginator path at src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:85-91, which converts datetime keys to ms and cursor values back to datetime
contracts.before_after: DateTimePaginator converts datetime to a float of milliseconds before floor/ceil, and converts the cursor value back to an aware datetime. OptimizedCursorPaginator does neither.
contracts.visible_effect: Response rows are never produced; 500 instead
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError from math.floor(datetime) in build_cursor for any non-empty page; the timestamp-vs-integer comparison in SQL fails for any cursor request

contracts.action: Slice the queryset with a negative start offset
contracts.before_after: Before: any negative offset raised in the QuerySet slice. After: the base path clamps forward cursors; prev cursors and the optimized branch still pass negatives.
contracts.visible_effect: 500 for crafted cursors with a negative offset
contracts.failure_mode: Django QuerySet raises ValueError on negative indexing

summary:
This PR shouldn't merge as it stands, for two reasons:

- **The new optimized path never works.** `OptimizedCursorPaginator` uses the integer `Paginator` key on the `datetime` field. `math.floor(datetime)` raises a TypeError, so every non-empty page returns 500. Its cursor values are also never converted back to datetimes.
- **The default path regresses.** `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is now read on every request. Any caller whose context has no member (and isn't a superuser) gets a 500, even without the new query parameter.

The negative-offset feature can't work: Django refuses negative QuerySet slices, so those cursors also return 500. The comments claiming it is safe and handled by the ORM are false. The permission gate checks `request.user.is_superuser` rather than `is_active_superuser(request)`, and `has_global_access` is true for most members by default, so the gate is not limited to administrators. The forward-cursor clamp in `BasePaginator` is harmless, but its comment is wrong. The PR adds no tests.
